research_question: Can class-Mondrian calibration preserve normalization's reduction in ambiguity while repairing its non-stress undercoverage on the independent wearable cohort?

fixed_model_and_representation.normalized_representation: Experiment 13 per-subject median/IQR normalization using heldout onboarding windows only
fixed_model_and_representation.nonconformity_score: one minus predicted probability for each candidate class
fixed_model_and_representation.marginal_rule: one pooled threshold from all 256 external calibration scores
fixed_model_and_representation.class_mondrian_rule: one threshold per true calibration class, each from 128 scores

interpretation_contract.pass: Class-asymmetric calibration is a supported repair component, conditional on every safety and usefulness check.
interpretation_contract.average_only: Class conditioning repairs aggregate or class coverage but not subject-level safety; retain class asymmetry as partial mechanism only.
interpretation_contract.fail: Class conditioning does not explain the external normalization safety failure; move to subject-level reliability or distribution-shift mechanisms.

guardrails: Do not alter features, classifier, subjects, folds, onboarding windows, test windows, alpha, or score definition.
Do not tune thresholds after viewing Experiment 14 outcomes.
Do not use heldout test labels for normalization, model fitting, threshold estimation, or arm selection.
Do not promote aggregate coverage when class or subject safety fails.
Do not claim literature novelty from this within-project follow-up.
No LLM or API call is permitted or required.
